posts.title: Making Number Gacha
posts.subtitle: Does a gacha game still work without its sexy anime girls?
body: Last month I released Number Gacha, a game where you roll, unpack, and battle numbers. Thank you to everyone who’s played! In my inaugural blog post, I wanted to look back on the project that has consumed the last six months of my life and figure out why it’s struck such a chord.

Let’s take a step back and start with this question. Is it slowly mastering a skill, or a satisfying progression of power? Is it a well-written, emotional story? Is it the thrill of shooting that last annoying enemy in the face?

These things are all fun— of course they are. These things are all fun— of course they are. But lately, I’ve been drawn to a different kind of engagement, one that feels cheaper. Games that include virtual roulette wheels or shiny loot boxes, where every rare item I get triggers a hit of dopamine in my brain. Why is something so crudely stimulating, such thinly veiled gambling, just as fun to me as a “real game” Why is something so crudely stimulating, such thinly veiled gambling, just as fun to me as a “real game”?

It feels akin to doomscrolling, trying to rack up as much stimulation as possible to keep my brain happy and sedated. Perversely, it actually started to make sense. I’m tired after a long day, or want to take a break from working and need something fast and quick. Why work for my fun through difficult, rewarding gaming when it can be served to me by a single click?
